# The frida:// URI grammar

Every rz-frida operation that involves a device is addressed by a URI:

```text
frida://<action>/<transport>/<device>/<target>
```

## The parts

| Part | Values | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| action | `list` `apps` `attach` `spawn` `launch` | what to do |
| transport | `local` `usb` `remote` | how to reach the target |
| device | empty, device id, `host:port` | see the table below |
| target | pid, process name, package name, executable path | required by `attach` `spawn` `launch`, must be empty for `list` `apps` |

Per-transport device rules:

| Transport | Device field |
|---|---|
| `local` | must be empty |
| `usb` | empty (single connected device) or a device id |
| `remote` | non-empty and must contain a `:` (host:port) |

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[action] -->|list, apps| E[target must be empty]
    A -->|attach, spawn, launch| T[target required: pid, name, package or path]
    T --> TR[transport]
    TR -->|local| D1[device empty]
    TR -->|usb| D2[device empty or device id]
    TR -->|remote| D3[device host:port]
```

## Examples

```text
frida://attach/local//1234
```

Attach to local pid 1234. Note the double slash: the device field is empty,
then the target.

```text
frida://spawn/usb//com.example.app
```

Spawn a package on the single USB device.

```text
frida://attach/remote/127.0.0.1:27042/4321
```

Attach to pid 4321 through a remote frida-server.

```text
frida://launch/local///bin/ls
```

Launch `/bin/ls` locally. The target starts with a slash, so there are three
slashes: after the empty device field, the target itself begins with `/`.

## Validate without touching a device

`fridau` parses and validates a URI without contacting anything. This is
useful for scripts and CI:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridauj frida://attach/local//1234
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","transport":"local","device":"","target":"1234"}}

[0x00000000]> fridauj frida://attach/usb//Gadget
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","transport":"usb","device":"","target":"Gadget"}}

[0x00000000]> fridauj frida://spawn/local///bin/ls
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"spawn","transport":"local","device":"","target":"/bin/ls"}}
```

Invalid combinations are rejected with `invalid_uri`:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridauj frida://launch/remote//bad
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"invalid_uri","message":"invalid Frida URI"}}

[0x00000000]> fridauj frida://attach/local//
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"invalid_uri","message":"invalid Frida URI"}}
```

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting the target for `attach`/`spawn`/`launch` → `invalid_uri`
- Giving a target to `list`/`apps` → `invalid_uri`
- A remote device without a colon → `invalid_uri`
- A device name on the local transport → `invalid_uri`
- Percent-encoding: none exists, write the URI literally
- A path with slashes: an absolute path needs the extra slash,
  `launch/local///bin/ls`. A relative path does not,
  `spawn/local//./native_demo`

> **Note:** `fridaoj` accepts a bare URI without the `frida://` prefix and
> adds it. `fridau`, `fridap`, and `fridaa` require the full form.
